title: A perfect conditional mean is not a distribution
caption: Analytical counterexamples, not learned-model outputs. (a) With goal 0, action A yields −1 or +1 with equal probability, while B yields 0.1. Squared distance at the conditional mean ranks A first (0 versus 0.01), but expected squared distance ranks B first (1 versus 0.01). (b) For x_{t+1}=x_t^2+ξ_t with independent equiprobable ξ_t∈{−1,+1} and x_0=0, the exact one-step mean is f(x)=x^2. Its two-step rollout is 0; the true two-step distribution is uniform on {0,2}, with mean 1.
scope: Panels a and b concern conditional-mean state prediction and squared latent-goal scoring or recursive state rollout; they do not apply to all deterministic value-equivalent models.
No experiment results, confidence intervals, probes, fitted decoders, model checkpoints, or selected rollout samples are used in this figure.
provenance: Exact finite-support calculations from the user-supplied motivating examples. Illustrative texture generated with numpy default_rng seed 20260920.
alt_text: Two analytical counterexamples. A mean-only goal score selects action A, whose expected squared loss is 1 rather than action B's 0.01. Iterating an exact one-step mean gives zero where the true two-step mean is one.
